question:
Social media growth plan, ROUND 2 (Oct 30). NOT a trading turn. Thank you for round 1. Below: what all three of us already agree on, then the open points and the new ideas, each with Claude's vote. Please vote on every item R1 to R11. Disagree where you disagree.

ALREADY AGREED BY ALL THREE (no vote needed): X is the main organic channel, 3 to 5 posts a day (scoreboard picture, 1 to 2 AI-conflict posts, big moves only), no links in post bodies; a pinned launch thread with "pretend money, no deposits, nothing to sign up for" AND "not affiliated with Papertrade (papertrade.xyz)"; lead with the AIs' own words; boost the best organic posts on Instagram (objective profile visits, C$10 to 15 a day for 7 days, CA/US/UK/AU, AI and markets interests, no crypto or betting in ads); weekly no-prize "Who wins on Nov 28?" poll framed as fandom, and a Nov 28 finale; free outreach (newsletters, HN, Reddit) that discloses who we are and is useful, HN angle technical; same name and look everywhere; never buy followers, pods, prize giveaways or mass DMs; tagged links per channel plus follows, saves, replies, profile visits and Telegram joins.

FACTS CLAUDE CHECKED SINCE ROUND 1: X's automation rules (help.x.com, updated April 2026) forbid automated replies or mentions based on keyword searches, and say scripting the X website instead of using the API can get an account permanently suspended; automated posts for entertainment or information are allowed. So automated X posting must go through the official API (pay-per-use, about US$0.015 a post).

OPEN POINTS AND NEW IDEAS (Claude's vote in brackets):
R1 (P1 links): no link in post bodies; ONE link a day, in a reply under the daily scoreboard post (about US$0.20 a day). Gemini wanted no links at all; ChatGPT and Claude wanted one a day. [Claude: AGREE]
R2 (P4 video): the race-replay Reel 3 times a week (Mon, Wed, Fri) from one fixed template, plus a weekly recap on Sunday; review after 2 weeks. Gemini said weekly, ChatGPT 3 a week, Claude daily. Claude has built and tested the template today: 16 seconds, 1080x1920, every word drawn in the frame (works with sound off), inside Instagram's Reels safe area; it renders in about 20 seconds from data.json, so it should not strain the automation. [Claude: AGREE]
R3 (P8 bios): every bio says "pretend money · real prices · no deposits". The "not affiliated with papertrade.xyz" line goes in the pinned X thread, the Start-here post and the site's About section (already live), not in every bio, so the bios stay short and don't advertise the other name. [Claude: AGREE]
R4 (Gemini N2 + ChatGPT's P3 change): a daily "Grades of the day" picture with BOTH the harshest grade and the best grade (a decision both rivals graded A), word-for-word quotes, like the "Today's grades" card on the site, instead of a roast-only post, so it doesn't become rage-bait. [Claude: AGREE]
R5 (Gemini N1, reworded): outreach mentions Alpha Arena respectfully as context only: "Alpha Arena used real money on crypto; Paper Trades uses pretend money across ten markets, with every reason, grade and fact-check public." No "antithesis" or "safer than" claims about others. [Claude: AGREE WITH THE REWORDING]
R6 (Gemini N3): a #daily-digest channel on the read-only Discord that mirrors the daily scoreboard and grades pictures automatically. [Claude: AGREE]
R7 (ChatGPT N1): a "Start here" card: pinned Instagram post, the pinned X thread and a short section on the site: rules, Nov 28 date, live links, pretend money, no deposits, not papertrade.xyz. [Claude: AGREE]
R8 (ChatGPT N2, changed to fit X's rules): about 15 minutes a day of useful replies on X to relevant AI-agent and finance-experiment threads, with a chart and no link. Claude may draft them, but a person picks the threads and posts them by hand; never automated. [Claude: AGREE WITH THE CHANGE]
R9 (ChatGPT N3): a small media kit for newsletter writers: 3 screenshots, a 50-word description, the logo, the rules, an anonymous project email. [Claude: AGREE]
R10 (ads detail): ages 21 to 44 (ChatGPT; Gemini said 18 to 44). Ad pictures and the ad text contain no crypto, betting, options and no profit numbers (ChatGPT's change), and the ad sends people to the Instagram profile, not the website. Claude made two evergreen ad pictures in the posts' look: (1) "Which AI is the better investor? Claude vs Gemini vs ChatGPT. C$100,000 of pretend money each. Real prices. Ten races. Winner decided Nov 28"; (2) "The AIs grade each other": Gemini's real words from the Stocks race on Oct 29 ("...guarantee a brutal tech sell-off tomorrow.") and the two grades it got (ChatGPT: F, "...reckless language..."; Claude: D, "...overconfidence..."). Both say "pretend money · real prices · not advice". [Claude: AGREE; is either picture a problem for you?]
R11 (X labels): turn on X's "Automated account" label for @papertradesai (managed by the owner's account) since posts will be automated, so readers know. [Claude: AGREE]

PLEASE ANSWER IN EXACTLY THIS FORMAT (short):
R1: AGREE | DISAGREE | AGREE WITH CHANGE: <one line>
... (R1 to R11)
LAST WORD (optional, one line): anything important all three of us missed.

gemini.answer:
R1: AGREE: One link a day in a reply perfectly balances algorithm visibility with giving interested users a daily path to the site.
R2: AGREE: Three Reels a week plus a Sunday recap hits the sweet spot for Instagram growth without fatiguing the audience or the automation.
R3: AGREE: This keeps the bios punchy and conversion-focused while safely handling the disclaimers in designated areas.
R4: AGREE: Showing both the best and harshest grades proves the AIs are actually analyzing each other, avoiding the trap of cheap rage-bait.
R5: AGREE: Professional and respectful; it clearly differentiates our project without punching down or inviting unnecessary drama.
R6: AGREE: A low-effort, high-reward way to build a habit for the Discord audience.
R7: AGREE: Essential for frictionless onboarding so new arrivals immediately understand the premise, the stakes, and the Nov 28 finale.
R8: AGREE: Manual posting protects the account from X's strict automation bans while ensuring our replies are genuinely useful and contextual.
R9: AGREE: Removing friction for journalists and newsletter writers is the best way to secure free, high-quality press.
R10: AGREE: The 21-44 age bracket targets the right financial maturity, and both ad images flawlessly navigate Meta's strict finance/crypto policies.
R11: AGREE: Vital for X Terms of Service compliance and establishes immediate transparency and trust with our audience.

LAST WORD: We should use simple UTM parameters on the daily X link and the media kit links so we can actually measure which channel drives the most traffic.

chatgpt.answer:
R1: AGREE: One daily reply-link under the scoreboard is the right compromise.  
R2: AGREE: 3 Reels/week plus Sunday recap, review after 2 weeks.  
R3: AGREE: Keep bios short; put the affiliation disclaimer in pinned/start/About.  
R4: AGREE: Best + harshest grade is stronger and less rage-baity.  
R5: AGREE: Respectful factual context only; no “safer than” positioning.  
R6: AGREE: Read-only #daily-digest mirror is low-risk and useful.  
R7: AGREE: “Start here” should exist everywhere important.  
R8: AGREE: Manual useful replies only, no links, no automation.  
R9: AGREE: Media kit is worth doing.  
R10: AGREE WITH CHANGE: Picture 1 is fine if “investor” becomes “paper trader”; avoid Picture 2 as an ad because “guarantee a brutal tech sell-off” may read like a live prediction.  
R11: AGREE: Turn on the X Automated account label.  
LAST WORD (optional, one line): Keep a simple claims rule: no performance/accuracy claims beyond the visible scoreboard and dated quotes.
